description: One thing that travelled across a handoff — or did not: what it was, what kind of thing it is, and (for an item that was lost) why it never reached the next agent. The record is a VALUE: the same type describes what a step passed on and what it lost, so a host builds one list of PassedItems and one of LostItems and the surface renders both from the same shape. Reason is only read on a LOST item; on a passed one it is ignored (a passed item does not need an excuse). Nothing here carries colour: the kind is an enum the surface turns into an icon and a localized word, and the lost/passed distinction is carried by the LIST an item lives in plus an icon and a word, never by a tone alone (WCAG 1.4.1).

members.name: Lost
members.description: Copies the item as a LOST one: the same label and kind plus the reason it never arrived. A host builds a LostItems list from the items it wanted to pass with this helper.

members.name: HasKnownKind
members.description: Whether Kind is one of the declared kinds (a cast integer may not be).

members.name: HasLabel
members.description: Whether the host supplied a label worth printing.

members.name: HasReason
members.description: Whether the item carries a reason worth printing (only a lost item renders it).

members.name: Kind
members.description: Which kind of thing it is; painted as an icon AND a localized word.

members.name: Label
members.description: What was handed over, as the host wants it read. Empty renders the surface's own fallback.

members.name: Reason
members.description: Why this item never reached the next agent ("the context window was full", "the tool was not granted"). Only read on a LOST item; empty renders no reason. A passed item keeps whatever the host stored and the surface ignores it.
